### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5ec398dccb77bc7ef954fc831c83babfbaced236`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5ec398dccb77bc7ef954fc831c83babfbaced236` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `490b04b855eba181f3096b85ecdc79c17dd3e5cf` — the merge of head `f5f4f537c195565fe234fbff91ad5f9cf0920da3` into base `5ec398dccb77bc7ef954fc831c83babfbaced236`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 490b04b855eba181f3096b85ecdc79c17dd3e5cf && git checkout 490b04b855eba181f3096b85ecdc79c17dd3e5cf
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5ec398dccb77bc7ef954fc831c83babfbaced236 f5f4f537c195565fe234fbff91ad5f9cf0920da3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5ec398dccb77bc7ef954fc831c83babfbaced236 && git merge --no-ff f5f4f537c195565fe234fbff91ad5f9cf0920da3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5ec398dccb77bc7ef954fc831c83babfbaced236
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5ec398dccb77bc7ef954fc831c83babfbaced236` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Read at 2026-10-27T22:44Z: card #26898 (body, triage `6453626118`, claim `6453886440`, os-dev-report `6455350411`), PR #26947 (body, 6-file list, net diff `origin/main...f5f4f537` over merge base `57820085fa`), and the head's 45 check-runs. `record-recognisers --paths` on the six paths returns no `hits` (no governed path); the committed changeset's `(narrowing)` arm decides the narrowing face, so the floor is every path outside the prose faces, listed first above.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set, dispatcher `GET /data/:object/:id` (narrowing) — right.** `data.ts` :280-284 at the head asks `unknownQueryParamRefusalMessage(query, DATA_RECORD_READ_PARAMS)` and answers any key outside `select` / `expand` with `deps.error(msg, 400, { code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' })`; on `main` the branch kept the two names and dropped the rest (`200`). The set is the one declared at `rest-server.ts` :633 (`['select', 'expand']`, the #7606 docblock), imported, not copied; the sentence is `query-allowlist.ts` :185-196 (unknown names sorted, allowed names sorted), the same function `refuseUnknownQueryParams` :214-219 writes for `RestServer`. `details.code` is promoted into `error.code` by the dispatcher's envelope builder (`http-dispatcher.ts` :1150-1166), the shape `data.ts` :447 already used, so the wire is `{ success:false, error:{ code:'VALIDATION_ERROR', message } }` as the PR says. Both hosts hand the querystring verbatim (`adapters/hono/src/index.ts` :543-551 `readDispatchQuery`, `dispatcher-plugin.ts` passes `req.query`), so no host-injected key can trip the closed set.

2. **Public surface, `@objectstack/rest` (widening) — right.** `index.ts` :84-87 adds one value export, `DATA_RECORD_READ_PARAMS` (`readonly string[]`), re-exported from `rest-server.ts`. Dependency edge: `packages/runtime/package.json` :43 already declares `@objectstack/rest: workspace:*`; `packages/rest/package.json` names no `@objectstack/runtime`; `data.ts` :38-41 already imported `assertFilterParamSuppliedOnce` and `repeatedQueryParamMessage` from the same entry. No new edge, no cycle, `packages/spec/**` untouched. Nothing exported is removed or narrowed.

3. **Gate order, and the seat's Q2 — right, with one unpinned status read from code.** `data.ts` :280 now calls `refuseUnexposedDataAction(..., 'get', ...)` (default `disabledPackage: 'defer'`) before the closed set, and `callData` (`action-execution.ts` :505) asks it again with `'refuse'` before the read. So on a served read it runs twice; that is the pattern the `query` (:242), `update` (:355) and `create` (:472) branches have carried since #23574, and the docblock at :423-430 names it ("Extracted from callData, which still asks it first for every caller"). The second run is cost only: `readExposureDeclaration` (:353-375) is a pure by-name metadata read (`protocol.getMetaItemForExecution` / `getMetaItem`, else `metadata.getObject`) with no audit, log or metric, and the refusal is one `Error` from `exposureRefusalFields` both times; a first-gate throw ends the request, so no second refusal shape exists. Status versus `main` for an unexposed object: `apiEnabled: false` answers `404 OBJECT_API_DISABLED` with and without `?nope=1` on both `main` (the dropped name never reached the gate) and the head (the first gate throws); pinned on the dispatcher by the rig's last `it`. One status does move, read from code: an object whose owning package is disabled (`OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`) with an unknown name answered `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` on `main` (name dropped, `callData`'s `'refuse'` threw) and answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` at the head (`'defer'` swallows the refusal at :477-480, the closed set answers first). That is the declared `'defer'` contract (:400-406: a malformed request is answered `400` first on that object) and what `RestServer` does (`enforceApiAccess` reads it as "no declaration" via `loadObjectItem`, then `refuseUnknownQueryParams` `400`, `crud-routes.ts` :201-214), so parity holds; it is not pinned (the rig's `RestServer` has no metadata store), flagged in ③.

4. **Hidden row and missing id — right.** The refusal precedes `callData`, so `?nope=1` on `HIDDEN` and `NOWHERE` answers `400` on the dispatcher as `RestServer` answers it before `p.getData` (`crud-routes.ts` :214). Information leak direction is the safe one: the exposure gate still runs first (point 3), and a readable-vs-hidden row is not distinguished by this refusal on either host.

5. **Parity rig (Q3) — pins what the card wants.** `data-record-read-status-parity.test.ts` at the head: 19 `CASES`; `it.each` asserts `{status, code, field}` equal to `expected` on each host and `message` equal across hosts (:231-241), so status, `code` and the sentence are pinned for an existing id (`MINE`), a missing id (`NOWHERE`) and an unreadable id (`HIDDEN`) with `?nope=1`, plus `?select=title&nope=1`, `?fields=title`, `?nope=1&selct=title`. Controls `?select=title` and `?expand=parent` (a `lookup` field `parent` was added so `expand` has a relation) stay `200`; the #26816 cases are unchanged. The REST reader was taught the nested `{ error: { code, message } }` body the closed-set gate writes (:191-194) so the comparison is on one shape. `http-dispatcher.test.ts` :1587-1603 flips the unit pin from "dropped" to "refused, `getData` not called", with the exact sentence (`"filter", "malicious"`, sorted). Red-on-base (6/13), green-after (19/19) and the `if (false && …)` ablation are the dev's; CI's `Test Core` shards were still running at read time (below).

6. **Census of the dispatcher's other `/data` routes (Q4) — the claim holds at the head.** `route-ledger.ts` :622-627 lists six `/data` rows. In `crud-routes.ts` the only `refuseUnknownQueryParams` call is the by-id route (:214): list `GET /data/:object` (:113-135) hands the whole query to `findData` after `enforceApiAccess`; `POST /data/:object` (:251-262), `POST /data/:object/query` (:321-342) and `PATCH /data/:object/:id` (:394-435) read no querystring; `DELETE /data/:object/:id` (:503-536) asks `refuseRepeatedQueryParams(['expectedVersion'])` (arity only) and reads nothing else. The dispatcher side matches (`data.ts`: list asks `assertFilterParamSuppliedOnce` only, query/create/update read no query, delete reads `expectedVersion` with the arity gate). No `RestServer` closed set exists for any of the five, so no host split. The one closed set `RestServer` does declare elsewhere on `/data`, `DATA_EXPORT_PARAMS` (`rest-server.ts` :636-672, `GET /data/:object/export`), has no dispatcher twin at all (`data.ts` has no export branch), which is the dev's second observation: on a dispatcher-only host that path reaches the by-id branch with id `export`, `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` before and `400` naming `format` now, both refusals of a route that host never served. Correctly left unfiled.

7. **Docs — matches the behaviour.** `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx` :215 now says any other parameter is refused `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` and "the message names it and lists the two accepted ones": `unknownQueryParamMessage` (:159-172) names the refused parameter(s) and ends `Supported parameters: expand, select.` The parameter table below it is unchanged and still right.

8. **Base drift.** `main` moved from the merge base `57820085fa` to `5ec398dccb`; of the cited files only `rest-server.ts` changed (a `metaMemberSelector` comment and the layered `/meta` request, #26699), nothing near `DATA_RECORD_READ_PARAMS` or the by-id route; the PR reads `mergeable: true`.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset** `.changeset/26898-by-id-read-unknown-param-refused.md`: `@objectstack/runtime: patch`, `@objectstack/rest: patch`, `fix(runtime)!:` title, `**BREAKING**` banner, Before/Now/Unchanged and a remedy. Both declaration lines present and identical to the PR body: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Level — right.** AGENTS.md §Post-Task Checklist 3 (ruling A, restated in `clause2-line.mjs` header): the level follows the metadata-protocol kind alone; `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". No authorable key, value or type moves here, so `none` is honest and `patch` on both moved packages is the rule's answer. (The older #16421 note in `clause2-line.mjs` :111-112 that `yes` "takes at least minor" is superseded by ruling A in the same file's header and by AGENTS.md; `Check Changeset` on the head read "LEVEL AXIS ok, patch".)
- **Clause-② grade (Q1) — `yes (narrowing)` is right, ruled from the line's reader.** `clause2-line.mjs` :89-90: the value answers one question, 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」 (`execution-duties.md` :67 is the same sentence). A new value export on a published package's entry is an expansion of the public surface, so the value is `yes`; the dispatcher door's accept set shrinks, so the arm is `(narrowing)`. `yes (narrowing)` is the reader's documented combination for exactly this shape (:113-114: "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. Both facts are true and both are read"). `no (narrowing)` would record only the narrowing and understate the diff; the precedent the dev cites, commit `8024e1243a` (#23072, dispatcher half), declared `yes (narrowing)` for two new `@objectstack/rest` entry exports plus a dispatcher narrowing, and landed. The claim's "likely `no (narrowing)`" was a forecast the dev was told to measure; the measurement is right and the departure is explained in the report.
- **ADR-0087 disposition (Q5) — holds.** Marker (an HTML comment in the changeset body) `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) …`, a category in `CATEGORIES` (`check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` :548-554). That category is refused only when the changeset body itself carries a migration prescription (a FROM → TO rewrite table or a framed `## Migration` region, :147-154 and :880-920); the body's "The remedy" is a request-side sentence (send only `select` / `expand`), no rewrite table, no framed heading, and no exported declaration is removed or narrowed, so none of `runtime-interface-only`, `type-surface-only` or `runtime-export-retired` is owed. The comment's "other categories are closed on facts" paragraph is accurate. `Check Changeset` (pr-automation.yml :998-999 runs `check-adr-0087-registration --base MERGE_BASE`) concluded `success` at 2026-10-27T22:40Z on this head.

The changeset's "Unchanged" bullet speaks of `apiEnabled: false` only, which is accurate as written. No rig case covers the disabled-package shape; a follow-up pin is optional and nothing here blocks landing.
